---
title: Main-text figure and table plan
---

This is a publication planning document. It identifies the role of each
display; it does not select final results, change estimates, or approve a new
fuel analysis.

## Main-text figures

| Working figure | Purpose in manuscript | Thesis source | Publication action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Study design | Orient readers to the Jackson Demonstration State Forest study area and treatment/sampling layout. | `analysis/thesis/methods.qmd`, Figures 2.1–2.2 | Retain one clear design figure; consider moving the second map/layout figure to supplement if the combined design can remain legible. |
| Regeneration response | Show redwood and tanoak understory density/basal-area response to overstory retention. | `fig-regen-ba-rw-to` in `analysis/thesis/results.qmd` | Retain and simplify as the lead results figure; omit secondary species classes from the main figure unless essential. |
| Sprout development | Show treatment and temporal/10-year patterns in redwood and tanoak sprout height. | `fig-sprout-ht-inc-treat`, `fig-sprout-ht-inc-year`, `fig-sprout-ht-yr-10` | Retain the management-relevant treatment and height/time findings in the main text. Combine displays only if the combined figure preserves both messages clearly. |
| Fuel conditions and PCT contrast | Report disaggregated fuel components before and after PCT, by retention target, including the PCT-associated contrast. | `fig-fuel-pct-comparison` | Promote to a main-text figure after the publication-specific component specification and summary/model review. Show phase estimates and uncertainty; retain comparisons that clarify the management implications of PCT or overstory retention. |
| Fuel-component detail | Provide additional phase-specific component detail when it cannot be read from the central comparison figure. | `fig-fuel-pre-pct`, `fig-fuel-post-pct` | Redesign or retain one only if needed to interpret the central PCT comparison; otherwise place the expanded display and full values in the supplement. |

The working target is four main-text figures, with a fifth available for a
separate sprout-height or fuel-component display if it is needed to preserve a
distinct management message.

## Main-text tables

| Working table | Purpose in manuscript | Thesis source | Publication action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Treatment and sampling design | Give treatment labels, retained-overstory targets, plot replication, and measurement timing. | `analysis/thesis/methods.qmd` | Create a compact new table; do not reproduce procedural detail already visible in the design figure. |
| Regeneration summary | Provide the small set of estimated values needed to support the lead regeneration figure. | `tbl-regen-ba-grand-means`, sprout tables in `analysis/thesis/tables.qmd` | Create only if figure annotations cannot communicate the estimates adequately. |
| Fuel conditions and PCT contrast | Provide disaggregated fuel-component values, units, phase, uncertainty, and the pre/post-PCT contrast. | Fuel mean and grand-mean tables in `analysis/thesis/tables.qmd` | Create after the publication-specific fuel definitions and summaries are finalized; place the complete reusable values in a supplement or data file if the table is too wide for the main text. |

## Supplementary displays

The supplement is the default location for the current detailed model listings,
dispersion/hurdle specifications, full pairwise-comparison tables, optional
Douglas-fir detail, secondary sprout figures, and expanded fuel-component
tables. This preserves reproducibility without requiring each item to carry the
main silvicultural and PCT-management narrative.
